slots.title: Factory PMI 54.6 missed 55.2 forecast
slots.body:
August ISM manufacturing PMI: **54.6** vs **55.2** expected (July **55.6**).

New orders **53.7** vs **56.0** expected.

Employment **51.2** vs **52.5** expected — still above 50, which separates expansion from contraction.

U.S. indexes closed lower the same session:
- $SPY proxy ^GSPC **-0.7%** to **7,632.60**
- Nasdaq ^IXIC **-1.0%** to **26,099.77**
- Russell 2000 ^RUT **-1.2%** to **2,920.13**

The fear gauge ^VIX **+9.5%** to **16.34**.

What factory line are you watching most ahead of payrolls data later this week?

slots.title: Job openings 7.27M, quits below forecast
slots.body:
July **JOLTs** job openings: **7.27M** vs **7.30M** expected (June revised **7.18M**).

Quits: **3.06M** vs **3.21M** expected (prior **3.21M**).

Openings still outnumber unemployed by a wide margin in this release — the question is whether quits keep cooling.

Same day, S&P Global manufacturing PMI for August printed **53.9** vs **53.2** expected — a beat on that separate survey.

Does a sub-7.3M openings print change how you read labor tightness?

slots.title: Bessent: China alone blocked G-20 export line
slots.body:
At the G-20, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said China did **not** join language opposing “non-market based economies” pushing “cheap exports.”

He pointed to China’s large current account surplus as context for the split.

Separately, WSJ reported the summit closed with bond-market pressure, tariff disputes, and public friction among ministers — no shared fix on deficits or inflation in that coverage.

U.S. session close (Sep. 1):
- ^GSPC **7,632.60** (**-0.7%**)
- 10-year Treasury yield **4.7%** (Aug. 28 snapshot)
- 2s10s spread **0.39** percentage point

Which G-20 thread matters more for your macro read — trade language or bond yields?

slots.title: Dell down 6.9% after EPS beat
slots.body:
$DELL closed at 424.68, down 6.9% (-31.33) on the session.

Reported EPS was 7.04 versus a 4.91 estimate; revenue was about $46.97B versus roughly $44.89B estimated.

The print landed the same day the S&P 500 fell 0.7% and the Nasdaq fell 1.0%.

How much of today’s move do you tie to the numbers versus the broader tape?

slots.title: Palo Alto falls 5.2% after beat
slots.body:
$PANW finished at 362.09, down 5.2% (-20.04).

EPS came in at 1.02 versus a 0.978 estimate; revenue was about $3.41B versus roughly $3.35B estimated.

Other software-linked names were lower on the same close:
- $MDB -4.2% to 434.21
- $GTLB -3.1% to 45.09

$ORCL was down 5.3% to 141.26 with no earnings line in today’s calendar.

When the report beats and the stock sells off, what do you look at first — guidance, multiples, or the macro day?

slots.title: US session recap — Sep. 1, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed at 7,632.60, down 0.7% (-53.54), with an intraday range between 7,611.20 and 7,663.63.

The Nasdaq Composite lost 1.0% to 26,099.77; the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.8% to 52,766.88; the Russell 2000 was off 1.2% to 2,920.13.

The VIX rose 9.5% to 16.34, from a 14.92 prior close.

August ISM Manufacturing PMI printed at 54.6 versus a 55.2 estimate (prior 55.6).
New orders were 53.7 versus a 56.0 estimate.

JOLTs job openings for July were 7.271M versus a 7.3M estimate; job quits were 3.056M versus a 3.21M estimate.

The Atlanta Fed GDPNow reading for Q3 was 4.8% versus a 4.6% estimate.

On sector averages (NASDAQ), Utilities led at +2.6%; Financial Services, Industrials, and Real Estate were each about -1.1% to -1.2%; Communication Services was +1.1%; Technology was +0.3%.

Oil exposure showed strength in the cross-asset set: the United States Oil Fund ($USO proxy) rose 5.5% to 141.00; Brent crude was up 1.0% to 95.57.
Headlines in the feed tied fresh US–Iran strikes to oil price action.

Gold futures (GCUSD) fell 0.8% to 4,359.30.
The dollar proxy (UUP) ticked up 0.3% to 28.21.
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was down 0.2% to 77,216.30.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-08-28) showed the 10-year at 4.7% and the 2s10s spread at 0.39.

Megacap earnings that reported on the calendar included Dell (EPS 7.04 vs 4.91 est.; revenue ~$46.97B), Palo Alto (EPS 1.02 vs 0.978 est.), MongoDB (EPS 1.9 vs 1.62 est.), GitLab (EPS 0.24 vs 0.18 est.), and MiniMed (EPS 0.12 vs 0.12 est.).
$DELL still closed -6.9%;:
- $PANW -5.2%
- $MDB -4.2%
- $GTLB -3.1%
- $MMED +10.7%

Healthcare-heavy names were firmer among large caps:
- $JNJ +2.0% to 271.19
- $UNH +1.8% to 396.30
- $ABBV +1.4% to 259.99
- $V -1.8%
- $MA -1.4%

Overseas indexes in the feed were lower: Nikkei 225 -2.6%, Hang Seng -1.1%, FTSE 100 -0.3%.
